_comment: National organizations that publish chapter or group directories. These matter more than hospices for two reasons: they cover the loss types hospices don't (child, suicide, overdose, infant, military), and those are exactly our highest-intent, lowest-competition search pages.
_access_policy: Check each source's robots.txt and terms of service BEFORE writing an adapter. Where automated access is not clearly permitted, use the manual CSV path in scripts/ingest/import_csv.py instead. Several of these organizations would likely welcome a data-sharing conversation - asking costs one email and is the better first move for the large ones.

_status_key.unchecked: No robots.txt or ToS review yet. Run check_source_access.py.
_status_key.automate: robots.txt permits our paths; adapter may be written.
_status_key.manual_only: Automated access unclear or disallowed. Curate by hand.
_status_key.contact_first: Large enough that a data-sharing request should be sent before anything else.

sources.name: The Compassionate Friends
sources.notes: The authority on child loss. Highest-value single source we have - child loss is our best long-tail page and hospices barely serve it. Peer-led chapters, almost always free, usually monthly.
sources.robots_note: robots.txt permits crawling, BUT: (1) the chapter locator is JavaScript-rendered - the HTML contains no chapter data, only a widget calling an internal API; (2) the page states the locator 'is not to be used for any kind of solicitation of TCF's Chapters'. We would not be soliciting, but reverse-engineering an internal API to extract their chapter database is a different act from crawling public pages. Moved to contact_first 2026-08-06. Write to the national office.

sources.name: American Foundation for Suicide Prevention
sources.notes: Well-maintained finder. Suicide loss is high-intent and almost unserved by hospices. Requires the crisis banner and careful copy - see the sensitivity rules in the verification policy.
sources.robots_note: NO CRAWLABLE GROUP PAGES. Re-verified 2026-08-23. robots.txt does say 'Allow: /' and the sitemap index is real, but sitemap-0.xml contains exactly FOUR urls matching 'support-group', all of them informational: /find-a-support-group/, /information-for-support-group-facilitators/, /facilitating-a-suicide-bereavement-support-group/ and /chapter/find-a-support-group. There is no page per group. The finder is an Astro widget - the served HTML reads 'Select an option above to show support groups' and the ~400 groups are returned by an internal API only. The earlier note here ('use the sitemap to enumerate group pages') was written when this source was catalogued and was never verified; it was wrong. Same category as TCF and NACG: reachable by asking, not by crawling.

sources.name: National Alliance for Children's Grief
sources.notes: The Dougy Center network. Nearly the only structured source for children's and teen grief support, which almost no directory covers well.
sources.robots_note: CLIENT-SIDE PAGINATION. Confirmed 2026-08-07: /page/2/ and ?sf_paged=2 both return byte-identical content to page 1 - only the first 12 of 652 are ever in the HTML. The pagination links are decorative; the real paging is an AJAX call. Same category as TCF and AFSP. Reachable only via a headless browser or by asking NACG directly. They publish a 'add or update your listing' form, so they clearly want the directory used - ask before engineering around it.

sources.name: Bereaved Parents of the USA
sources.notes: Complements Compassionate Friends. Expect overlap - dedupe on address and meeting time.
sources.robots_note: BEST AUTOMATABLE SOURCE FOUND. Verified 2026-08-23. The path recorded here previously (/chapters) 404s; the real one is /find-a-chapter/. That single static HTML page carries EVERY chapter, grouped under state headings, with chapter name, leader, phone, email, and sometimes a street address and meeting schedule. One request, no pagination, no JavaScript.
sources.privacy_note: Publishes volunteers' PERSONAL home addresses and personal email addresses (e.g. a leader's home street address in Jacksonville AR). Take chapter name, city, state and phone; link back to bereavedparentsusa.org for contact. Do NOT republish a volunteer's home address or personal email on a page we are actively driving search traffic to.

sources.name: GRASP (Grief Recovery After Substance Passing)
sources.notes: Overdose loss is badly underserved and carries heavy stigma, so people search privately rather than ask. High-intent, near-zero competition.
sources.robots_note: robots.txt returned empty twice. Rather than assume, treat as manual_only and use the CSV import path. ~40 groups is a couple of hours of hand-curation, and overdose loss is too valuable a category to skip on a technicality.

sources.name: Share Pregnancy & Infant Loss Support
sources.notes: Often hospital-affiliated, so cross-reference with health system pages.
sources.robots_note: Verified 2026-08-23. Real HTML, no bot blocking, and the site publishes 'Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=yes' - an explicit opt-in. The chapter data sits behind 50 per-state expanders on /find-a-share-chapter-near-you; a click did not expand the section in the accessibility tree, so the expander target still needs identifying before an adapter is written. Site says 'over 65 Chapters in 29 states'.

sources.name: MISS Foundation
sources.notes: Founded in Arizona. Natural first outreach call - a local relationship is worth more than a scraped page, and they may share data directly.
sources.robots_note: Only wp-admin disallowed; support directory permitted. Still worth a phone call first - they are Arizona-founded and a local relationship beats a scrape.

sources.name: Soaring Spirits International
sources.notes: Widowed community, skews younger than hospice bereavement groups. Fills a real gap.
sources.robots_note: MUST honor Crawl-delay: 5 - five times slower than our 1s default. Also disallows ALL query strings (/*?*), so any adapter must use clean sitemap URLs, never search parameters.

sources.name: TAPS (Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors)
sources.notes: Mostly national rather than local, but matters for San Diego and San Antonio.
sources.robots_note: Not yet checked - lowest priority, mostly national rather than local programs.

sources.name: GriefShare
sources.notes: By far the largest network, but three cautions. (1) Volume would swamp everything else and unbalance our metro pages. (2) Christian and curriculum-based - must be tagged accurately so people who want secular support aren't misled. (3) Large enough that we should ask before taking anything. Deliberately last.
sources.robots_note: robots.txt has an empty 'User-agent: *' block with no rules, which technically permits crawling. Status deliberately stays contact_first - 900 groups in our metros would swamp every page, and an organization this size deserves to be asked.

_finding_2026_08_23: The large national directories gate their group data behind JavaScript; the small ones publish plain HTML. TCF (500), NACG (652), AFSP (400) and GriefShare (8000) are all JS-gated - about 1,550 US groups that no amount of crawling will reach. BPUSA (60), Share (65), MISS (40) and Soaring Spirits (50) are plausibly crawlable, roughly 215 groups. Engineering buys the small half; the large half has to be asked for. Send the outreach email.
